_about: Language data for chronology/what-languages-declare.md, read by utils/build_languages_graphics.py. Every figure carries its source; Biblical dates are not stored here -- they come from docs/data/chronology.json.

world.source: Glottolog 5.3 (2026-03-02), https://glottolog.org/glottolog/glottologinformation; the 7,674 total reproduced from the glottolog-cldf v5.3 languages.csv

lineage_sizes.source: glottolog-cldf v5.3 languages.csv: spoken L1 languages per top-level family (excluding the sign, pidgin, mixed, artificial, speech-register, unattested, unclassifiable and bookkeeping pseudo-families); 238 families hold a language in this count, the other 8 of the stated 246 do not

lees_1953.source: R. B. Lees, 'The Basis of Glottochronology', Language 29 (1953) 113-127

swadesh_1955.source: M. Swadesh, 'Towards Greater Accuracy in Lexicostatistic Dating', IJAL 21 (1955) 121-137

retention.chance_floor_note: approximate level below which look-alikes cannot be told from chance; drawn dashed

diversification.source: language counts: Glottolog child_language_count for each family (includes recorded extinct varieties); ages: when the parent began to split

families.name: Arabic
families.age_note: the 7th-century AD conquests; Glottolog's Arabian node holds 38, less Ancient North Arabian, which is pre-Islamic and no daughter of it

families.name: Slavic
families.age_note: Common Slavic, from the 6th-7th century AD

families.name: Narrow Bantu
families.age_note: the Bantu expansion, c. 3000 BC, a model date

scripts.source: conventional dates and descent, as in P. T. Daniels & W. Bright (eds.), The World's Writing Systems (1996) and Woodard (2004); 'dashed' marks a disputed link; 'near' marks an origin within about 1,000 km of Jerusalem (Uruk ~990 km, Abydos ~700 km, Serabit el-Khadim ~350 km)

first_writing.source: conventional dates (middle chronology for Mesopotamia) as given in R. D. Woodard (ed.), The Cambridge Encyclopedia of the World's Ancient Languages (2004) and the works named per row; BC; 'dashed' marks a date or an identification that is disputed

rows.what: Abydos tomb U-j labels (reading as language disputed)
Sargonic royal inscriptions (Semitic names at Fara are earlier)
names in the Kanesh merchant archives (Kloekhorst 2019; Yakubovich 2010)
Mitra and Varuna in the Mitanni treaty with the Hittites
oracle-bone inscriptions, reign of Wu Ding
